newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN DOMINATES, TOMBA GOES OUT.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN DOMINATES, TOMBA GOES OUT.

text.p: Switzerland's Michael Von Gruenigen looked unbeatable at the Alpine skiing world championships on Wednesday, leading after the first leg of a giant slalom that ended Alberto Tomba's hopes.
Tomba's long-awaited debut at the championships lasted around one minute and ended, as many had feared, in failure for the 30-year-old giant and slalom world champion.

The Italian showman, starting 16th after last month losing his place in the top 15 giant seeds for the first time in a decade, lost his balance at the top of the icy Sises 2 piste, recovered and then got into even greater trouble.
He skidded on a curve and almost came to a stop as he fought to regain control entering a flat section.
Tomba then had to use his poles to regain speed but, realising it was a useless endeavour, called it a day and skied off the piste to come to a halt by the side.
Tomba said everything had gone badly for him. "I'm very sorry. But Saturday will be my day," he said.
He added that he felt positive about Saturday's slalom, having won the last World Cup race before Sestriere, but complained that it and the giant were too long.
He also complained that he had been tired and the play of light and shade on the course had made matters harder. The leg was set by Norwegian Max Valquist with 61 gates.
Before Tomba's run, six of the seeded 15 had gone out.
Von Gruenigen, bronze medallist in giant and slalom last year and winner of two World Cup giants this season, started first and made it all look relatively effortless.
The World Cup giant champion led the first leg by 1.12 seconds ahead of second placed compatriot Steve Locher with the fastest time of one minute 23.31 seconds.
"I was glad that I started first because I could have my own line," Von Gruenigen said. "It was definitely an advantage on the upper part of the course."
Norway's Lasse Kjus was in third place, 1.28 behind Von Gruenigen and in with a good chance of his third medal of the championships after silvers in downhill and super-G.
Norwegian Kjetil-Andre Aamodt, winner of the men's combined event, was in fourth 1.37 seconds off the pace with Austrians Rainer Salzgeber and Hans Knauss joint fifth in 1:24.75.
Switzerland's Urs Kaelin was the first casualty, losing an edge and crashing out after a fast start.

Other frontrunners who went out included Slovenia's Jure Kosir, Austrian Siegfried Voglreiter and French duo Ian Piccard and Christophe Saioni. Italy's Matteo Nana, another local favourite, lost about four seconds after nearly falling.
